summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with ESRD on hemodialysis, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, atrial fibrillation, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for chest discomfort and nausea that occurred during dialysis. The symptoms were attributed to demand ischemia due to elevated heart rate and blood pressure, not a myocardial infarction. She converted from atrial fibrillation to sinus rhythm, had two inpatient hemodialysis sessions, and responded well to adjusted medication timing—specifically taking metoprolol on dialysis mornings while holding lisinopril and diltiazem. Her INR was supratherapeutic, so warfarin was held pending outpatient recheck. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated medication instructions and plans for outpatient follow-up, including an EMG for decreased left hand grip strength.
